claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask you a few questions.

**First, let's start with your child's age:**

How old is the child you're claiming for? The age determines the basic eligibility requirements:

- **Under 16**: Generally qualifies automatically (subject to other conditions)
- **16-19**: May qualify if they're in approved education or training
- **20 or over**: Generally not eligible

Could you tell me your child's age?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes - I'm looking to claim for my child Alex. He's 13 years old and lives with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information! Let me continue with the assessment for Alex, who is 13 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Since Alex is 13 years old (under 16), he's in the automatic qualification age range. Now I need to check a few more conditions.

**Next question about Alex:**

Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?

(This is a standard check - at 13, it's unlikely he'd be working full-time, but I need to confirm this to proceed with the assessment.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all - he's just in school like a normal 13-year-old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Alex is in school and not working. 

**Next question:**

Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

In other words, is he free from receiving these types of benefits personally? (Again, this is very unlikely for a 13-year-old in school, but I need to confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a regular school kid.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now another quick check:

**Is Alex NOT in an apprenticeship?**

Since you mentioned he's just a regular school kid at 13, I assume he's not in any apprenticeship program, but I need to confirm. (For context, certain types of apprenticeships can affect eligibility, but this varies by region - England, Scotland, and Wales have different rules.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any apprenticeship - he's only 13, so he's just in regular school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me move forward with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your residency status. You mentioned you live in the UK with Alex.

**Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You'll meet this requirement if **ANY** of the following applies to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this is the most common scenario)
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and are working (earning above the National Insurance threshold)
4. You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work (up to 91 days)
5. You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources to support yourself
6. You have pre-settled status as a student with sufficient resources
7. You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national
8. You're a Crown servant living abroad or in certain qualifying countries

Which of these applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK - I live here with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You meet the residency requirements. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex.

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You're considered responsible if **ANY** of the following applies:

1. **You live with Alex** (which you've already mentioned you do)
2. You contribute to Alex's upkeep (paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards their care - including food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents)
3. You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement

Since you mentioned Alex lives with you, that satisfies the responsibility requirement. Is that correct - Alex lives with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check about other potential claimants.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member
- Anyone else who might have applied

Please let me know:
- Is there no other claimant?
- Is there another claimant but you've both agreed that you should be the one to claim?
- Is there a dispute about who should claim?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to understand Alex's living situation a bit more.

**Which of the following best describes where Alex is living?**

- **Living normally** with you at home (standard situation)
- In hospital
- In care (local authority care)
- Fostered

Since you mentioned Alex lives at home with you and is just a regular school kid, I assume he's living normally with you - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - he's just living normally at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Just one final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you paying for Alex's living costs yourself (without the local council contributing)? 

This is typically straightforward - if Alex lives with you and you're supporting him without local authority financial assistance for his care, the answer would be yes.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - I'm paying for everything myself. The council isn't paying anything towards his care.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Let me get the final outcome for you.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News - You're Eligible for Child Benefit!

**Result: ELIGIBLE**

You meet all the Child Benefit eligibility requirements for Alex. Based on our assessment:

✅ Alex is 13 years old (under 16 - automatically qualifies)
✅ He's not working full-time (he's in school)
✅ He's not receiving benefits in his own right
✅ He's not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
✅ You normally live in the UK (residency requirement met)
✅ You're responsible for Alex (he lives with you)
✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
✅ Alex lives normally at home with you
✅ The local council isn't paying towards his care

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge**: If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit through tax
5. **Payments**: Child Benefit is paid every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

### How to Apply:

You can find the claim form and apply here: [https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim)

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit or the application process?

reasonings: Alex is eligible for Child Benefit because: (1) He is 13 years old, which is under 16 and automatically qualifies for the age requirement; (2) He is not working 24+ hours per week - he's just in school; (3) He is not receiving benefits in his own right such as ESA or Universal Credit; (4) He is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship - he's in regular school; (5) The claimant meets UK residency requirements by normally living in the UK; (6) The claimant is responsible for Alex as they live together; (7) No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex; (8) Alex is living normally at home; (9) The local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. All eligibility criteria have been met.
